title: Chapter 49
content:
The ground floor was already bustling with early morning visitors.

Curious about the commotion, Jakyeong drifted downstairs to find Kang Yu-jung, Kang Il-hyun’s older sister. With the formal inauguration scheduled for tomorrow, she explained that she had dropped by specifically to say goodbye to Jang Yi-an before his imminent departure.

"Oh, Yi-an... I’m going to miss you so much. Please stay healthy and take care of yourself."

She pulled Jakyeong into a warm, gentle embrace. A light, delicate fragrance drifted from her skin—reminiscent of fresh wild blossoms. Unconsciously letting his guard down, a relaxed, boyish smile spread across Jakyeong's face.

Over her shoulder, his eyes caught Kang Il-hyun sitting on the living room sofa.

Il-hyun was glaring straight at him, deliberately dragging a thumb across his own throat in a slow, lethal slit-throat gesture.

Jakyeong broke the hug in a flash, taking a hasty step back. "Th-Thank you, Noona. You be careful of your neck... I mean, take good care of your health."

Hearing the affectionate title, Yu-jung’s lips curved into a touched, delighted smile. What a dream it would be to have such a sweet, handsome little brother, she thought. Between her two actual younger brothers, one was a ruthless, cold-blooded machine, and the other was a reckless, spoiled degenerate.

Taking Jakyeong by the hand, she guided him to the sofa and presented an exquisitely wrapped gift box finished with a pristine silk ribbon.

"Open it. I really hope you like it."

He untied the ribbon and peeled back the paper, revealing a handcrafted wooden music box carved into an ornate, miniature carousel. For someone like Jakyeong, who harbored a secret fondness for charming, delicate objects, the gift was an absolute strike.

"Thank you, Noona. Truly... I love it."

"I'm so glad."

Having grown up without ever owning proper toys as a street urchin, Jakyeong had always held a quiet, lingering attachment to small trinkets. In a way, perhaps it sprang from the exact same psychological deprivation that drove Kang Il-hyun’s twisted fixation on nipples.

Beaming down at the little wooden horses, Jakyeong caught Il-hyun’s eye across the table—sure enough, the bastard was watching with a cold, mocking smirk.

Yu-jung turned to her brother with a puzzled frown. "Aren't you going into the office today?"

"It's Sunday."

Dressed in tailored slacks and a crisp, collared shirt without a tie, he was dressed formally enough that mistaking it for a workday ensemble was entirely natural.

Yu-jung gave Jakyeong a cheerful demonstration of how the mechanism worked. Winding the brass key beneath the base, a bright, crystalline melody began to play as the carousel spun. The tune was hauntingly familiar, though the exact title eluded him.

As Jakyeong and Yu-jung chatted and laughed over the melody, Il-hyun watched the display with narrowed, venomous eyes, finally pushing himself up from the sofa and disappearing into the master suite.

After Yu-jung departed, Jakyeong headed up to his room to pack.

Tossing out the bulk of Jang Yi-an’s wardrobe—clothes he would never wear again—cut his luggage in half. Opening the nightstand drawer, his eyes landed on the luxury watch Kang Seok-joo had gifted him days ago. Childish, arrogant, and constantly running his mouth... but not fundamentally rotten to the core.

He set the timepiece onto the marble top and resumed packing when a soft knock broke the quiet.

The door clicked open, and Kang Il-hyun strolled inside. Settling on the edge of the mattress, he looked down at Jakyeong kneeling over his duffel bag on the hardwood floor.

"Packing your things?"

Jakyeong gave a curt nod. "Yes. Almost finished."

"Departing the country immediately after the trigger date, I take it?"

"Most likely."

"And the remaining balance?"

"Wire it to the same offshore account as the advance," Jakyeong replied, folding a shirt. "Handing me a duffel bag of cash wouldn't do me much good at airport customs anyway."

It was a redundant exchange, covering terms they had already settled days ago.

Il-hyun’s eyes drifted across the room, catching the wooden music box sitting atop the bedsheets. He picked it up by the roof, turning it over in his hand.

"Forgot to pack this one."

"Ah—"

Jakyeong held out an open palm, asking for it back.

Instead, Il-hyun casually opened his fingers, letting the music box plummet toward the floor.

Jakyeong lunged to catch it mid-air, but a fraction of a second too late.

The wooden casing struck the hardwood with a hollow crack.

Jakyeong’s face twisted into an instant, murderous scowl.

Il-hyun stared down at the wreckage, his lips curling into an unapologetic, deeply satisfied smirk. "My, my. My hand slipped. My apologies."

Jakyeong dropped to his knees, picking up the carousel. One of the finely carved wooden horses had sheared cleanly off its brass pole. He glared up at Il-hyun with pure venom. Vindictive until the bitter end.

"You should have caught it properly," Il-hyun drawled, enunciating every word with deliberate spite. "Since it's such a precious keepsake."

Precious keepsake. The sarcastic edge cut like a razor.

Jakyeong had thought the man had turned over a new leaf after playing the polite gentleman for the past two days. He wound the brass key under the base; the crystalline melody still played clearly through the tines. A little wood glue will fix the horse easily enough.

Swallowing a string of curses, Jakyeong tucked the music box deep into the padded center of his duffel bag.

For some inexplicable reason, Il-hyun slid off the mattress and sat flat on the hardwood floor right beside him. Crossing his long legs, he fixed a heavy, unblinking stare on Jakyeong’s face.

Zipping up his gear, Jakyeong finally looked up. "What?"

Il-hyun didn't answer right away, his dark eyes slowly tracing every contour of Jakyeong's features. Those eyes truly are exquisite. A shame they'll rot away in the dirt once he's buried. Maybe I really should have him preserved...

"I think I'm going to miss you."

The quiet confession was laced with an uncharacteristic, lingering warmth.

Looking into those dark pupils, Jakyeong felt as though he understood the emotion—and at the same time, understood nothing at all. Rather than probing the madness, he offered a faint, ambiguous smile and went back to tightening his luggage straps.

Il-hyun remained seated on the floor, watching him in dead silence until the final buckle clicked shut.

Waking before dawn, Jakyeong showered and took a final sweep of the guest suite. Checking for anything left behind was standard tradecraft, but beneath the protocol, twenty days under this roof had left a strange, lingering familiarity.

Stepping into the upper foyer, Park Tae-soo was already waiting by the banister.

"Allow me, Young Master. I will carry your bag down."

Even knowing full well that the man before him was not the real Jang Yi-an, Tae-soo maintained the deferential facade to the very end.

Jakyeong followed him downstairs, bidding farewell to the domestic staff. The senior housekeeper pulled him into a tight, lingering embrace, her eyes wet with maternal reluctance. It was a completely different warmth from Yu-jung’s—cozy, grounding, and deeply comforting. It brought back vivid memories of Wang Han’s late grandmother, making a faint prickle rise behind his eyes.

"It would have been wonderful if the Director had been here to see you off," she murmured softly. "He had to leave at dawn for the inauguration proceedings."

"It's quite alright, ma'am. We exchanged our goodbyes yesterday."

After offering a final, respectful bow, Jakyeong stepped outside. While Tae-soo stowed the duffel in the trunk, Jakyeong slipped into the rear leather seat.

He glanced up at the sprawling villa through the tinted glass. The estate that had felt so foreign and suffocating when he first arrived now looked remarkably familiar. As the sedan rounded the driveway and cleared the iron gates, he kept his eyes on the receding estate until the mountain road swallowed the view.

Tae-soo drove in complete, stoic silence for the entire thirty-minute transit—a fitting finale, considering Jakyeong had rarely heard more than three consecutive sentences from the man during his entire stay.

The car pulled to a stop near a designated suburban intersection. Tae-soo stepped out, opened the rear door, and retrieved the duffel from the boot.

Taking the strap, Jakyeong offered a polite nod. "Thank you for everything, Chief Park."

Tae-soo returned a crisp, silent bow.

"You can head back first. I'm meeting a companion here."

"Understood, sir."

Tae-soo climbed back into the sedan and merged into traffic.

Once the tail-lights disappeared around the bend, Jakyeong wheeled his bag toward an unassuming black hatchback idling outside a convenience store.

He tapped on the driver's window: Tap-tap.

Wang Ryun rolled the glass down, popped the hatchback, and helped stow the gear inside. He jerked his chin toward the road where Tae-soo’s car had vanished.

"That guy just now... was that Kang Il-hyun?"

"No. His chief of security."

"What time does the ceremony kick off?"

"Eleven hundred hours."

Ryun pulled a set of cloned license plates from the footwell, quickly swapping them out over the originals. With the swap complete, the two climbed inside and merged onto the expressway toward central Seoul.

Ryun cranked the stereo, headbanging aggressively to a blaring hip-hop track with absolutely zero sense of rhythm. Watching the chaotic performance, Jakyeong couldn't help letting out a genuine laugh.

In the passenger seat, Jakyeong pulled a black utility cap low over his brow, swapped his shirt for a plain dark tee, and pulled on a high-visibility yellow utility vest. Emblazoned over the left chest was the corporate logo of an HVAC maintenance contractor. He hung a forged technician ID badge around his neck and turned his gaze out the window.

Traffic ground to a halt along the Mapo Bridge, drawing a sharp, irritated hiss from Ryun. "Fucking morning rush hour... an absolute parking lot."

While the car was idling, Jakyeong pulled a compact hard case from his tactical backpack and handed it across the console.

"Returning the gear."

Ryun popped the latches, inspected the interior foam, and scowled. "What the hell? There's a micro-transmitter missing from this kit."

"Couldn't retrieve it."

"Do you have any idea how much that prototype cost?!"

"Ten percent," Jakyeong said flatly.

Ryun threw his hands up in mock exasperation. "Ugh, always with the damn ten percent! Take any more out of my cut, and you'll be asking for my liver and kidneys next!"

Despite the grumbling, Ryun’s expression hardened into focused steel as they approached the city center. Jakyeong’s throat felt dry as bone; he cracked open a bottle of mineral water, took a measured sip, and checked his tactical watch.

One hour remaining until the strike window.

"Destination in sight," the GPS announced. Ryun leaned forward, whistling as he peered up through the windshield.

The commercial high-rise loomed overhead, soaring so high it strained the neck to see the crown.

"Which floor did you say?"

"Seventeenth."

"You sure about this? Shouldn't you pack a parachute just in case?"

Jakyeong smirked, adjusting his cap. "Keep the jokes for the ride home."

"Make it back in one piece," Ryun said, holding out a closed fist.

Jakyeong bumped his knuckles against Ryun's with a firm tap, grabbed his heavy steel tool case from the backseat, and stepped out onto the asphalt.

He strode through the revolving glass doors of the lobby, where a security guard immediately stepped forward to intercept him. Flashing his forged work order and contractor badge, the guard made a quick confirmation call and cleared him through the turnstiles.

Stepping into the elevator, Jakyeong hit the button for seventeen. A cluster of corporate employees were packed inside, chattering loudly about quarterly targets and market forecasts.

When the chime sounded on the seventeenth floor, Jakyeong stepped out into the carpeted corridor, keeping his brim pulled low. Moving past several closed corporate suites, he reached an unoccupied office suite bearing the brass plaque of Yuhan Construction.

He pulled the handle; the suite was unlocked and completely deserted.

Stepping inside, he latched the deadbolt securely behind him, crossed the bare concrete floor to the panoramic windows, and set the tool case down. Slipping the technician ID from his neck into his pocket, he surveyed the building opposite through a pair of compact tactical binoculars.

Across the street, the banquet hall for the inauguration was already swarming with high-profile attendees, private security details, and media crews.

Reaching into his pack, Jakyeong retrieved a high-tensile extraction cable, securing it around the reinforced concrete load-bearing pillar with an interlocking carabiner knot. He gave the line two hard, violent yanks, testing the load limit.

Satisfied, he leaned his back against the glass, lit a cigarette, and checked the digital display on his wrist.

Forty minutes until the shot.

He took a slow, deep drag, letting the smoke fill his lungs before grinding the ember out beneath his boot. Opening his mobile player, he put on a quiet, ambient instrumental track to center his focus.

Taking a slow, measured breath, he unlatched the heavy clasps of the tool case, exposing the compartmentalized high-density foam within.

He reached inside, drawing out the modular components of the heavy precision sniper rifle.

The icy, polished steel sent an electric chill through his fingertips.

Click. Clack.

The precision receiver, heavy match barrel, bolt assembly, and optic slotted together in seamless, fluid succession—each metallic snap echoing through the vacant concrete room like the quiet, inevitable approach of death itself.
